From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aurora.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Initial ask: geo-lock checklist and sample wipe proof for Dedicated

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aurora is close to finalizing the Dedicated contract but security needs concrete artifacts for our data residency and deletion requirements. Specifically we need:

- A checklist that maps Redwood's Dedicated deployment controls to Aurora's policy items (region-lock, no cross-region replication, snapshot retention windows, tenant isolation)
- One example artifact that demonstrates a tenant-scoped deletion (e.g., a minimal wipe-proof text output or log sample)
- Confirmation of SLA and timeline for purge requests (RTO/RPO-style language if possible)

Can you share those artifacts and confirm whether any of the steps require on-prem access or customer-supplied keys? James from procurement and our security team are looped in.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we need this for the security review by Mar 20.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Corp Security Lead, Aurora Systems
security@aurora.com

--
Attachment: requirements_summary.pdf (listed)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aurora.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: geo-lock checklist and sample wipe proof for Dedicated

Hi Maria,

Thanks — we can get that to you today. Attached is a short checklist (geo-lock-checklist.xlsx) that maps Redwood Dedicated controls to common customer requirements. Highlights:

- Region lock: Customers can pin Dedicated capacity to a single cloud region; snapshots and persistent storage are bound to that region.
- Replication: No automatic cross-region replication for tenant volumes in Dedicated unless explicitly configured for DR; we document the opt-in control.
- Tenant isolation: Logical tenancy plus node-level allocation; snapshots labeled with tenant ID and reachable only via the tenant's control plane tokens.
- Purge flow: We run a multi-stage purge: tombstone -> asynchronous scrub -> snapshot sweep. Expected completion for a standard tenant-initiated deletion is 48–72 hours for logical deletion, with physical storage reclamation dependent on snapshot retention policies (configurable).

I also attached a small text artifact (wipe-proof-sample.txt) that shows sanitized log lines and the minimal proof we provide for a completed tenant scrub. That file is a sanitized sample — not real customer data.

A few clarifications I want to call out so there's no surprises:
- KMS: If you supply a customer-managed KMS key (recommended for additional assurances), key destruction or key rotation decisions are customer-controlled. Redwood supports both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys.
- Backup retention: By default snapshots are retained for 30 days; we can shorten on a per-contract basis and include shorter retention in SOW.
- On-prem: No on-prem access is required for the standard purge/evidence flow. If Aurora requires on-site validation or witness scrubs, we can discuss a controlled process but that is extra.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the checklist and sample artifact; call out any items that need stronger language for your legal/security teams.
2) If acceptable, we can add the exact retention window and SLA into the SOW and generate a DocuSign for signature.

If helpful, Ben and David are available for a short technical call tomorrow to walk through the purge stages and provide a live demo of a sandbox deletion.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

--
Attachments: geo-lock-checklist.xlsx, wipe-proof-sample.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: technical clarifications before we send final artifacts to Aurora

Stephanie — quick notes after reviewing the checklist and sample:

1) The sample wipe proof currently demonstrates logical scrub + tombstone entry and a post-scrub event id. For Aurora we'll generate a second sample that includes the blob-hash and the snapshot meta indicating tenant ID and region tag. That should satisfy their forensics folks.

2) Snapshot retention: we should offer an explicit 7-day minimal retention option in the SOW (instead of 30) to make the default negotiable. Laura, can you add that as an option to the commercial redline?

3) KMS phrasing: define "customer-managed KMS" in the checklist as: "Customer controls key lifecycle; Redwood cannot access plaintext without explicit key unwrap operation authorized by customer." Keeps it short and auditable.

I'll prepare the additional sample by EOD and hand it to Stephanie to send. Also propose we include a short runbook appendix (one page) describing the purge request flow and timestamps customers will see in the console/log (request received -> tombstone created -> scrub started -> scrub completed).

Ben
Senior Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
